newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to oppose bond for Fla professor in child case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to oppose bond for Fla professor in child case.

text.p: U.S. prosecutors said Monday they would oppose bail for a Florida university professor accused of bringing a Honduran youth into the country illegally.
Assistant U.S. Attorney John McMillan said Marvin Hersh, a Florida Atlantic University mathematics and business professor, was considered both a danger to the community and a risk to flee.
In a hearing Monday, Magistrate Anne Vitunac set two future court dates for Hersh, a bond hearing for April 16 and a plea hearing April 24.
Hersh, 57, was charged with alien smuggling, passport fraud and lying to the U.S. Social Security Administration to obtain a Social Security number for the boy, who is now 17.

Hersh, who has been suspended from his university post, was arrested April 11 at his Boca Raton, Florida, home following a yearlong investigation by the U.S. Customs Service, the State Department and other federal and state agencies.
Hersh brought the youth from Honduras in August 1995 after promising the boy's mother that he would see the youth received an education, McMillan said.
Authorities initially believed the child was 11 but said a physician's examination and subsequent investigation in Honduras found the youth was actually 17.
He was placed temporarily in the care of the Florida Department of Children and Family Services.

While investigators found documents in Hersh's home relating to the professor's involvement with sex tourism and his international search for child sex partners, physicians found no signs of sexual abuse, according to prosecutors.

An affidavit filed by the U.S. Attorney's Office had alleged that Hersh, who enrolled the boy in elementary school and began adoption proceedings, had sex with the boy and his brother before bringing him from Honduras.
